original_question: Develop general lower bounds for the degree of higher secant varieties, analogous in spirit to the lower-bound framework used for second secant varieties.
target_in_paper: Part 1, §1.3, Problem 7: "Provide lower bounds for the degree of higher secant varieties, in the spirit of [CR06]." ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))

missing_details: The paper’s default ambient setting is projective geometry over the complex numbers; the draft does not state this.
The objects should be defined explicitly: for a projective variety X ⊂ PV, the r-th secant variety σ_r(X) is the Zariski (equivalently Euclidean) closure of the locus of points of X-rank at most r.
“Higher secant varieties” should be quantified as secant varieties σ_r(X) with r ≥ 3, since σ_2(X) is the comparison case discussed just before Problem 7.
To make the question stand-alone, one should specify that degree means the projective degree of σ_r(X) in its ambient projective space.
The nearby phrase “in the spirit of [CR06]” is not generic: the paper has just recalled the model bound that if X is non-degenerate and codim σ_2(X) = c, then deg(σ_2(X)) ≥ binom(c+2,2).

If one wants the question to stand alone rather than rely on nearby prose, the natural non-degeneracy hypothesis on X should be stated explicitly, because it appears in the motivating σ_2(X) bound quoted immediately before Problem 7.

No extra hypotheses about homogeneous forms, polynomial degree restrictions, nilpotency, ambient rings, or asymptotic clauses such as “for all sufficiently large m” belong here; adding them would make the question less faithful to the paper.
refined_question: Let X ⊂ PV be a non-degenerate projective variety over C, and for each integer r ≥ 3 let σ_r(X) denote the r-th secant variety, i.e. the Zariski closure of the locus of points of X-rank at most r. Find general lower bounds for the projective degree deg(σ_r(X)) of these higher secant varieties, in a way that extends to r ≥ 3 the second-secant lower-bound perspective recalled immediately before Problem 7, namely the [CR06]-type bound deg(σ_2(X)) ≥ binom(c+2,2) when c = codim σ_2(X).
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 7 in §1.3, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 1.3 first recalls a lower bound for the degree of the second secant variety from [CR06], then says “We propose two problems in this direction,” and Problem 7 is exactly “Provide lower bounds for the degree of higher secant varieties, in the spirit of [CR06].” The notation section and the opening of Part 1 provide the default field (complex numbers) and the definition of σ_r(X). By contrast, Problem 8 asks for classification/minimal-degree examples for second and third secants and hypersurface cases, so it is adjacent but different. ([agates.mimuw.edu.pl](https://agates.mimuw.edu.pl/images/notes_and_reports/Gesmundo_Geometry_of_Tensors_Open_Problems_and_Research_Directions.pdf))
